messages:
alice: Quick sketch: "adjacent-takeover" pattern for canary/A-B rollouts. Nearby replicas can briefly "absorb" traffic if a canary degrades. Lightweight per-cohort latch + gen counter. TTL suggestion 20s to start.

bob: By "absorb" do you mean a replica serves another variant's traffic or it proxies? How do we avoid divergence?

alice: Replica serves same variant if latch says it's stable; otherwise proxy to central adjudicator. We only allow short slices and require emit of a takeover event.

carla: Staleness risk is real. Propose adaptive TTL: shrink during error spikes (down to 2s) and expand when stable. Also include health_epoch in latch so others detect active transitions.

dave: Sidecar vs central adjudicator tradeoffs: sidecar = low latency and resilience to control-plane blips; central = global budget/safety. Hybrid seems best: sidecar fast-path, central authoritative reconcilier.

alice: API is small: decide(cohort_id, token) -> {variant, gen, source, reason}. Sidecar only returns latch if freshness ok, otherwise forwards.

bob: Where to store latch? in-memory sidecar map + small disk spill. Avoid network caches for fast path. Use LRU and per-tenant caps to bound memory.

carla: Telemetry: add a "takeover_seen" flag in rollout UI and emit newline-json events: {rollout_id, cohort, variant, gen, event: takeover|release, ts}. Console should show a short timeline.

dave: Safety circuit: central aggregator consumes sidecar events; if takeover_rate > threshold in window -> auto-block new canaries for that tenant until review. Keeps ops safe.

ops-bot: job: rollout/adjacent-takeover-poc queued by bob - est 25m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alice: Action items: 1) I'll add latch schema + adaptive-ttl to RFC draft. 2) carla to sketch event schema and UI bits. 3) dave to define safety thresholds. 4) bob to prototype sidecar LRU store. Thanks!
